text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland and Ukraine are strategic economic partners, Poland's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said after talks with Ukraine's Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko in Warsaw yesterday.
- Polish-Ukrainian reconciliation is fundamental to political stability in central and eastern Europe, the ZCHN Christian nationalist party leader Marian Pilka said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET NEWS.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Around 5,000 customs officers participated in the go-slow strike which led to 30 km jams on some border crossings yesterday.

- The U.S.'s Citibank, Korea's Samsung and a group of four Polish financial institutions will participate in privatisation of the Warsaw-based Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK), a source which declined to be named said.
- Autostrada Wielkopolska SA road construction firm will build a stretch of the A2 motorway from Swiecko, northwestern Poland to Strykow, central Poland, transport ministry official Jan Sawicki said.
- Consumer goods and services prices rose by 1.1 percent in February compared with January, which showed the lowest price growth since last August, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Poland's private corporate sector's revenues were 270.9 billion zlotys last year, while state-owned companies' revenues reached 272.2 billion, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- The Chinese-Polish Chipolbrok shipping firm earned a net profit of $1 million on revenues of $98 million in 1996, the company said.
- Poland's budget deficit in the first two months of this year reached 1.5 billion zlotys, the finance ministry said.

- Poland's Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek will visit seven provincial areas which applied for the establishment of special economic zones (SEZ) in the cities and towns of Tarnobrzeg, Zarnowiec, Slupsk, Kostrzyn, Olsztyn, Starachowice and Czestochowa to discuss the SEZ projects they produced.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland's economic ministers committee (KERM) has accepted the privatisation plan of the Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) telecom monopolist, to start in 1998.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland's foreign trade deficit in food products was $1.218 billion last year, a report by the Agricultural Assistance Programme Foundation (FAPA) said.
ZYCIE
- The listed ComputerLand software maker and systems integrator signed a cooperation agreement with Sanchez Computer Associates on supplying services to the banking sector.
PARKIET

- The Warsaw-based Bank Ochrony Srodowiska (BOS) environmental protection bank has sold 292,818 shares in the HS Wyszkow glassworks, which represented a controlling 86.05 percent stake. The bank declined to reveal financial details.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
